common_name: Paint the Town Fancy Dianthus (Proven Winners Fragrant Rosy Fuchsia Red-Eyed Interspecific Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Paint the Town Fancy is part of a Proven Winners dianthus series bred for cutting-length stems and extended bloom.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Paint the Town Fancy produces single, rosy fuchsia flowers with contrasting red eyes over a low, spreading mound of glaucous blue-green foliage, carrying a light clove fragrance and continuous bloom from early summer onward. As part of the Proven Winners Paint the Town series it was bred for extended cutting-length stems and heat tolerance beyond older dianthus hybrids. Give it sharp drainage and avoid heavy, wet soils, which it resents year-round.

common_name: Paint the Town Fuchsia Dianthus (Proven Winners Fragrant Fuchsia Lavender-Eyed Interspecific Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full to part sun; Paint the Town Fuchsia reblooms continuously from early summer into fall and can continue flowering through winter in warm zones.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full to part sun. Paint the Town Fuchsia bears single, vivid fuchsia flowers with contrasting lavender centers above a tight, low mound of blue-toned, salt-tolerant foliage that holds its color through winter. It flowers nearly continuously from early summer through fall and attracts bees and butterflies throughout its long bloom window. Keep soil on the lean and dry side, since prolonged moisture at the crown leads to rot.

common_name: Paint the Town Red Dianthus (Proven Winners Fragrant Deep Magenta-Red Interspecific Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Paint the Town Red is the deepest-colored member of the Proven Winners Paint the Town series.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun to light shade. Paint the Town Red produces single, deep magenta-red flowers with a sweet fragrance over a low mound of glaucous blue-green, evergreen-in-mild-winter foliage, blooming continuously from early summer onward. Its spreading habit suits border edging, rock gardens, and groundcover use, and it tolerates salt, heat, and brief drought once established. Avoid heavy or constantly damp soils, which quickly rot the crown.

common_name: Fruit Punch Cherry Vanilla Dianthus (Proven Winners Double Deep Red Pink-Edged Interspecific Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full to part sun; Cherry Vanilla is part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series bred for repeat bloom and improved heat tolerance.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full to part sun. Cherry Vanilla produces abundant double flowers in deep red edged with light pink, carrying a sweet fragrance on both bloom and foliage over a tight mound of blue-green leaves. It flowers heavily in spring and early summer with continued flushes through the season, drawing bees and butterflies throughout. Give it sharp drainage and let it dry between waterings, as it declines quickly in constantly wet soil.

common_name: Fruit Punch Classic Coral Dianthus (Proven Winners Fragrant Double Coral-Pink Interspecific Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full to part sun; Classic Coral blooms heavily from early summer through fall as part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full to part sun. Classic Coral bears fully double, fragrant coral-pink blossoms over needle-like, blue-green foliage that adds textural interest even out of bloom. It flowers heavily from early summer into fall and works equally well as a border edging plant, cut flower, or dried flower. Keep the soil lean and sharply drained, since this cultivar is intolerant of heavy or waterlogged ground.

common_name: Fruit Punch Funky Fuchsia Dianthus (Proven Winners Double Florist-Quality Fuchsia-Purple Interspecific Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun to light shade; Funky Fuchsia produces florist-quality double blooms as part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun to light shade. Funky Fuchsia produces fully double, fragrant fuchsia-purple flowers up to two inches wide over semi-evergreen, glaucous blue-green foliage, with a mounded habit suited to borders, edging, or mass planting. It blooms heavily in early summer with continuous repeat flowering, and the blooms hold up well as cut or dried flowers. Heat and drought tolerance are strong once established, but sharp drainage remains essential.

common_name: Fruit Punch Raspberry Ruffles Dianthus (Proven Winners Double Raspberry-Pink White-Edged Interspecific Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full to part sun; Raspberry Ruffles is part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series bred for extended bloom and cut-flower quality.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full to part sun. Raspberry Ruffles produces large, double raspberry-pink flowers edged in a thin ribbon of white over upright, blue-green, mounded foliage, blooming from early summer through fall. Its fragrant flowers are well suited to cutting and drying, and the plant draws bees and butterflies steadily through its long bloom season. Give it lean, sharply drained soil in full sun for the best flowering and fullest form.

common_name: Fruit Punch Sweetie Pie Dianthus (Proven Winners Semi-Double True Pink Dark-Eyed Interspecific Pink)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun; Sweetie Pie blooms nearly continuously as part of the Proven Winners Fruit Punch series.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Sweetie Pie bears semi-double, true-pink flowers with a darker pink eye over a low mound of silvery blue-green, near-evergreen foliage, with fragrant blooms that draw bees and butterflies. It flowers continuously from early summer into fall, and regular deadheading extends the display further. It works well as an edging or container filler and tolerates heat and brief drought once established.

common_name: Pretty Poppers Kiss and Tell Dianthus (Proven Winners Blush-to-White Red-Eyed Interspecific Pink)
scientific_name: Dianthus interspecific 'Pretty Poppers Kiss and Tell'

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in fall in very well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in part shade to full sun; Kiss and Tell is the debut release in Proven Winners' Pretty Poppers dianthus series, US Plant Patent 32,227.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in very well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in part shade to full sun. Kiss and Tell carries large, semi-double, fragrant flowers that open blush pink and fade toward white around a dark red eye, held over a compact, blue-green, mounded habit. It blooms in two distinct flushes, early summer and again in early fall, and tolerates salt and short dry spells once established. As the first Pretty Poppers release, it was bred for an unusually wide range of light tolerance for a garden dianthus.

common_name: SpinTop Red Starburst Blanket Flower (Dwarf Bicolor Pinwheel Gaillardia)

planting.note: Set out container-grown plants in spring, or in fall in mild-winter zones, into lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; a dwarf, well-branched SpinTop-line blanket flower.

directions: Grow in full sun in lean, gritty, very well-drained soil; SpinTop Red Starburst is a dwarf, well-branched blanket flower producing toothy-petaled blooms with a vivid red base radiating out to golden-yellow tips, giving each flower a distinctive two-toned pinwheel pattern. It stays compact under a foot tall, making it well suited to containers and sunny border edges, and it flowers from spring through summer with deadheading extending the show. Spent flower heads can be left into late season as a food source for birds. It is deer-resistant and tolerates heat and drought well once established, but needs sharp drainage to avoid crown rot.

common_name: Forged in Fire False Sunflower (Burgundy-to-Orange-Eyed Semi-Double Heliopsis)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in average, well-drained soil in full to part sun; Forged in Fire grows to medium height with an upright, dense, mildew-resistant habit (US Plant Patent 37,356).

directions: Grow in average to fertile, well-drained soil in full to part sun. Forged in Fire produces semi-double blooms whose dark burgundy centers shift outward into fiery orange tones, giving the flower a smoldering, two-toned look across its long summer-to-fall bloom season. The dark green, mildew-resistant foliage stays clean and dense on an upright plant that rarely needs staking. It tolerates heat and periods of dry soil once established, and its abundant flowers draw bees and butterflies throughout the season.

common_name: Rays for Days False Sunflower (Large Fully Double Golden Zinnia-Like Heliopsis)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in average, well-drained soil in full to part sun; Rays for Days is valued for unusually full, Zinnia-like double flowers.

directions: Grow in average to fertile, well-drained soil in full to part sun. Rays for Days produces large, fully double, golden-yellow flowers with a dense, Zinnia-like petal count, held on a compact, mounded plant that stays shorter than most heliopsis. Deadheading extends its already long midsummer bloom season, and the disease-resistant foliage holds up well in heat and average water conditions. Its abundant flowers are a strong draw for bees and butterflies and make good cut flowers.

common_name: Touch of Blush False Sunflower (Variegated Pink-New-Growth Semi-Double Yellow Heliopsis)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in average, well-drained soil in full to part sun; Touch of Blush is notable for white-and-green variegated foliage that emerges flushed with pink.

directions: Grow in average to fertile, well-drained soil in full to part sun. Touch of Blush pairs semi-double, golden-yellow, overlapping-petaled flowers with foliage unlike any other heliopsis: new leaves emerge white with dark green veining and a distinct pink blush before settling into green. It blooms over an unusually long window from summer through fall without requiring deadheading, on a compact, mounded, disease-resistant plant. Average water and somewhat dry soil tolerance make it adaptable to typical perennial border conditions.

common_name: Athena Gold False Sunflower (Compact Petal-Packed Golden Heliopsis)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in average, well-drained soil in full to part sun; Athena Gold is a compact Proven Winners selection with heavy, petal-dense flowering.

directions: Grow in average to fertile, well-drained soil in full to part sun. Athena Gold bears sunny yellow, densely petal-packed blooms over a compact, mounded plant that is more manageable in smaller borders than taller heliopsis selections. It flowers from summer through fall with easy care, tolerating somewhat dry soil and average water once established, and benefits from a winter mulch in colder zones to guard against freeze-thaw heaving. Its long bloom season and bee- and butterfly-friendly flowers make it a reliable mid-border or mass-planting choice.

common_name: Tuscan Gold False Sunflower (Showy Dark-Green-Leaved Golden Heliopsis)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in average, well-drained soil in full to part sun; Tuscan Gold is a Proven Winners selection grown as a companion to the earlier Tuscan Sun release.

directions: Grow in average to fertile, well-drained soil in full to part sun. Tuscan Gold produces sunny yellow, daisy-form flowers over dark green foliage on an upright, compact plant that blooms steadily from summer through fall. It shows outstanding disease resistance and tolerates somewhat dry soil once established, needing only occasional deadheading to sustain its long flowering season. Its bee- and butterfly-friendly blooms also hold up well as cut flowers.

common_name: Bacio del Sole False Sunflower (Golden-Orange Daisy-Flowered Heliopsis)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Bacio del Sole is a taller Proven Selections heliopsis bred for abundant golden-orange flower production.

directions: Grow in average to fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Bacio del Sole produces an abundance of rich golden-orange, daisy-form flowers from summer into fall over a mounded, low-maintenance plant that needs little more than occasional deadheading to keep flowering. Cutting the plant back after bloom keeps it tidy heading into winter. Its generous nectar-rich flowers draw bees, butterflies, and hummingbirds, and the plant resists deer browsing.
